title: Claude AI Tutorial for Beginners (Step-by-Step)
author: Kevin Stratvert
summary: The cleanest first nine minutes you can spend on Claude. Stratvert has spent years making software tutorials for ordinary office workers, and it shows: no hype, no jargon, just screen-share of signing up, sending a first message, attaching a file, and getting a usable answer. If you have never opened Claude and want one video before you start, this is it.
who_for: Complete beginners who have never opened Claude and want a calm, no-nonsense walkthrough of the interface before doing anything else.
skip_if: Skip if you already use Claude weekly. This stops at the basics and teaches nothing about Projects, files, or getting better output from harder tasks.

title: Full Claude Tutorial: Beginner to Advanced in 19 Minutes
author: Futurepedia
summary: A fast, well-edited tour that gets you from the chat box to the features people actually miss - Projects, file uploads, artifacts, and how to structure a request so Claude does not waffle. Good density per minute without feeling rushed. Works well as the second video after a pure beginner intro.
who_for: People who have poked at Claude a few times and want a structured map of what the product can do, in one sitting.
skip_if: Skip if you have never opened Claude at all - it moves too fast to be a true first video. Also skip if you want depth on one workflow rather than broad coverage.

title: FULL Claude Tutorial for Beginners in 2026! (Become a PRO!)
author: AI Foundations
summary: The most-watched independent Claude walkthrough on YouTube, and it earns the views. Roughly fifty minutes covering the whole product surface with real on-screen work rather than slides, including Projects, file handling, and how to keep Claude consistent across a long task. Long enough to be genuinely useful, short enough to finish in one evening.
who_for: Anyone who wants one thorough sit-down session that covers most of Claude rather than five scattered short videos.
skip_if: Skip if you only have ten minutes, or if you dislike the high-energy YouTube tutorial style with heavy editing and channel promotion between sections.

title: FULL Claude Tutorial For Beginners in 2026! (FULL COURSE)
author: Productive Dude
summary: Almost two hours, structured like an actual course rather than a video. The pacing is slow on purpose, so nothing gets skipped - each feature is set up, demonstrated on a real task, then reviewed. This is the one to pick if you learn by following along step by step and you would rather watch one thing properly than sample ten.
who_for: Methodical learners who want a single long course they can work through with Claude open in another window.
skip_if: Skip if you are impatient or already comfortable with chat AI tools - the deliberate pace will frustrate you, and the first half hour will be familiar.

title: Claude AI Step-by-Step: The Beginner's Blueprint for Real Results
author: Teacher's Tech
summary: Built on the honest premise that you only need a handful of habits to get real work out of Claude, not a hundred features. Teacher's Tech has a long track record explaining software to educators and older learners, and the tone here is patient and plain. Strong on the mental model of how to ask, weak on advanced features - which is the right trade for the audience.
who_for: Nervous or non-technical first-timers, especially teachers and older learners who want to be taught rather than impressed.
skip_if: Skip if you want feature coverage - Projects, Cowork, and Skills are barely touched. Also skip if you already write good prompts.

title: NEW: Claude's 'Super Prompts' Will Save You DAYS of Work (Full Tutorial + Demo)
author: AI News & Strategy Daily | Nate B Jones
summary: Nate B Jones is an analyst rather than a hype channel, and this is the rare prompting video that explains why a structure works instead of handing you a template to copy. He builds a long, layered prompt live and shows what each part is doing to the output. Twelve minutes that will change how you write every request afterwards.
who_for: People who already use Claude daily but get mediocre output and suspect the problem is how they are asking.
skip_if: Skip if you have never used Claude - this assumes you already know the interface. The title is louder than the calm, analytical content, so skip if that framing puts you off.
notes: 80K views, 12:00, verified 2026-08-22. From October 2025 - the prompting principles hold up, but the model version and UI shown are older than current Claude.

title: How to Use Claude Projects (Full Tutorial)
author: Kevin Stratvert
summary: Projects is the single feature that turns Claude from a chat toy into a work tool, and most people never find it. Six and a half minutes: create a project, upload your reference files, write the instructions once, and stop re-explaining yourself every conversation. Short, precise, and immediately actionable.
who_for: Anyone repeating the same background context to Claude over and over - marketers with a brand voice, teachers with a curriculum, researchers with a set of papers.
skip_if: Skip if you already use Projects. This covers setup only and does not get into organising a large knowledge base or when Projects is the wrong choice.

title: Learn 80% of Claude Cowork in Under 20 Minutes
author: Jeff Su
summary: The best single explanation of Cowork for people who do not write code. Jeff Su is an ex-Google productivity creator and his gift is cutting a feature down to the parts that matter for office work - here, letting Claude work across your actual files and folders instead of copy-pasting into a chat box. Clear diagrams, real tasks, no filler.
who_for: Knowledge workers who have heard Cowork mentioned and want to understand what it actually changes about their day.
skip_if: Skip if you want the remaining 20 percent - advanced setup, custom skills, and edge cases are deliberately left out. Also skip if you do not have a paid Claude plan, since Cowork needs one.

title: My Simple Claude Cowork System (for normal people)
author: Jeff Su
summary: The follow-up to his Cowork intro, and the more useful of the two once you are past setup. Instead of demoing features, Su shows the folder structure and file conventions he actually uses so Cowork stays reliable week after week. The 'for normal people' in the title is honest - nothing here requires technical skill, just a bit of tidiness.
who_for: People already using Cowork who find it inconsistent and want a repeatable system rather than one-off wins.
skip_if: Skip if you have not tried Cowork yet - start with his 20-minute intro instead. Skip too if you want a general Claude tutorial, since this is narrow by design.

title: The ONLY Claude Cowork Tutorial You'll Ever Need in 2026
author: Aishwarya Srinivasan
summary: Srinivasan is a working AI practitioner rather than a tutorial channel, and she is unusually good at explaining what Cowork is doing under the hood without making it technical. Twelve minutes covering how it differs from normal chat, where it genuinely saves time, and where it still falls over. The honesty about limits is what lifts this above the pack.
who_for: Professionals who want a credible practitioner's take on Cowork, including what it is not good at, before investing time in it.
skip_if: The title oversells - this is a solid overview, not the only thing you will ever need. Skip if you want a slow click-by-click setup walkthrough.

title: Claude AI for Researchers: Projects, Skills, Cowork & Consensus Explained
author: Andy Stapleton
summary: Stapleton is a former academic who has spent years reviewing research tools for PhD students, so he frames every feature around a real academic job - screening papers, drafting a methods section, keeping a literature set in one place. He also pairs Claude with Consensus for citation-backed searching, which is the sensible answer to Claude's weakness at finding real sources.
who_for: PhD students, postdocs, and academics who want the whole Claude feature set explained in research terms rather than business ones.
skip_if: Skip if you are not doing academic or literature-heavy work - the examples will not transfer. Also skip if you want deep coverage of one feature rather than a tour of four.

title: How To Use Claude For Academic Research (My Actual AI Stack)
author: Prof. David Stuckler
summary: A working professor showing the tools he genuinely uses, not a reviewer speculating. Nine minutes on where Claude sits alongside other tools in a real publishing workflow - drafting, restructuring arguments, responding to reviewers - and, importantly, where he refuses to use it. The credibility of the source is the main reason to watch.
who_for: Academics who want to see how a published researcher actually integrates Claude, including the boundaries he sets around it.
skip_if: Skip if you need step-by-step instructions - this is a workflow overview and assumes you can operate the tools yourself. Not useful outside academic writing.

title: 3 Mind Blowing Claude & Consensus Research Workflows | No Coding
author: Dr Amina Yonis
summary: Three concrete research workflows demonstrated end to end, with the sourcing problem handled properly - Consensus finds and verifies the papers, Claude does the reading and synthesis. Dr Yonis builds content for PhD students and keeps it strictly non-technical, which the title promises and the video delivers.
who_for: Researchers and graduate students who want copyable literature-review workflows and are worried about Claude inventing citations.
skip_if: Skip if you will not use Consensus - two of the three workflows depend on it. Skip if you want general Claude skills rather than research-specific recipes.

title: Claude Cowork for Academics: Full Setup & Use Cases
author: Andy Stapleton
summary: The best answer to 'what does Cowork mean for someone with a folder of two hundred PDFs?' Stapleton sets it up on a real academic file system and runs it across a paper collection, showing both the time saved and the places it misreads things. Practical setup detail that generic Cowork tutorials skip.
who_for: Academics with large local document collections who want Claude working on their files directly rather than through uploads.
skip_if: Skip if you do not keep your research as local files, or if you are still deciding whether to pay for Claude - Cowork requires a paid plan.

title: Claude AI for Teachers: Complete Beginner's Guide to Getting Started (Projects, Prompts & More)
author: Teaching With Intelligence
summary: Made by a practising high school teacher, which shows in the examples - differentiating a worksheet, drafting parent emails, building a rubric. Twenty-three minutes that assume no technical background and no prior AI use, and that treat classroom constraints as real rather than as an afterthought.
who_for: Classroom teachers starting from zero who want examples from their own job rather than generic office tasks.
skip_if: Skip if you already use AI in your teaching - the pace and level are aimed squarely at first-timers. Not useful for university lecturers or corporate trainers.

title: How Teachers Can Create Interactive Classroom Activities with AI (Claude Artefacts Tutorial)
author: RoarTech Education
summary: Artifacts let Claude build a working interactive activity - a quiz, a simulation, a drag-and-drop exercise - without you writing any code, and this is the clearest teacher-facing walkthrough of that. Twenty-six minutes of building real classroom material on screen, then adjusting it by asking in plain English.
who_for: Teachers who want to make interactive digital resources but have no coding skills and no budget for edtech tools.
skip_if: Skip if you only need text output like lesson plans and worksheets - Artifacts is overkill for that. From January 2026, so the interface has shifted slightly since.

title: Claude Design: The Complete Guide
author: UI Collective
summary: A design channel covering a design tool, which is rarer than it should be. Thirty-two minutes on Claude Design with the judgment a designer brings - where the output is genuinely usable, where it is generic, and how to push it toward a real design system rather than a pretty first draft. The critical eye is the value here.
who_for: Working designers evaluating Claude Design seriously, and anyone who wants a designer's opinion rather than a feature demo.
skip_if: Skip if you have no design background - the critique assumes you can tell good layout from bad. Skip too if you want Figma integration, which is not the focus.

title: Claude Design Tutorial for Designers | First Look + Full Walkthrough!
author: Nehmat Gereige | AI-Design Professor
summary: A design educator's first pass through Claude Design, recorded on launch week. Less polished than a scripted tutorial but more honest - you watch her work out what the tool does well and what it refuses to do, in real time. Good pairing with a more structured guide once you know the basics.
who_for: Designers who want an unvarnished first impression from someone who teaches design, before committing time to learning the tool.
skip_if: Skip if you want a clean reference tutorial - this is exploratory and occasionally meanders. Recorded at launch, so some rough edges shown have since been fixed.

title: Claude Code for product managers: research, writing, context libraries, custom to-do system, more
author: How I AI
summary: Despite the name in the title, almost nothing here is programming - it is a product manager using Claude to synthesise user research, maintain a context library, and draft documents. The show format is a live over-the-shoulder walkthrough of a real workflow, which is far more instructive than a slide deck about PM prompts.
who_for: Product managers who want to see a serious end-to-end Claude workflow for research synthesis and document drafting.
skip_if: Skip if the terminal intimidates you - the tool is command-line even though the work is not technical. Skip too if you want a quick tips list rather than 43 minutes of one person's system.

title: Claude Code for Product Managers with Sachin Rekhi
author: Reforge
summary: Reforge is a respected product-management education brand and Sachin Rekhi is a well-known PM voice, so this is the closest thing to an authoritative session on Claude for product work. An hour on prototyping ideas, pressure-testing specs, and using Claude as a thinking partner rather than a writing machine. Strategic framing, not tool tricks.
who_for: Experienced product managers who want the strategic case for AI in product work from credible practitioners.
skip_if: Skip if you are new to product management - the conversation assumes fluency in PM vocabulary. Skip if you want a hands-on tutorial, since much of this is discussion.

title: Claude Cowork: The Ultimate AI Agent for Writers (Full Tutorial)
author: The Nerdy Novelist
summary: The Nerdy Novelist has covered AI for fiction writers longer than almost anyone, and he tests tools against real manuscripts rather than demos. Here he points Cowork at a working draft folder - chapters, notes, style guide - and shows it holding continuity across files, which is the thing chat-window writing has always failed at.
who_for: Novelists and long-form writers managing a manuscript across many files who need consistency of voice and plot.
skip_if: Skip if you write short pieces - the whole advantage here is scale. Skip if you object to AI in creative writing on principle, since he does not debate that question.

title: Claude Cowork Just Changed How You Do Marketing
author: Ben AI
summary: Forty minutes of actual marketing production rather than theory - brand voice files, a content calendar, repurposing one asset into several channels, all run through Cowork against a real folder. The length is justified because he does not cut away from the messy parts where output needs correcting.
who_for: Marketers and content people who want to see a full campaign workflow built in Cowork, including the failures.
skip_if: Skip if you want a quick overview - this is a long working session. The title is overstated and there is channel promotion in places, so skip if that grates.

title: Anthropic Just Dropped Claude for Small Businesses (31 Skills)
author: Brock Mesarich | AI for Non Techies
summary: A walk through the prebuilt small-business skill set - bookkeeping, proposals, customer email, marketing admin - with an assessment of which ones are worth using and which are filler. The channel's whole premise is explaining AI to non-technical owners, and the pitch stays grounded in ordinary business admin rather than growth fantasies.
who_for: Small business owners and solo operators who want to know what Claude does for back-office work out of the box.
skip_if: Skip if you do not run a business - the framing is entirely commercial. The news-style title means the first minutes are announcement rather than instruction.

title: How to setup Claude for Small Business
author: Harry Davies
summary: Nine minutes of pure setup with no motivational padding - account, workspace, connecting your business documents, and getting the first useful output. This is the practical companion to broader overview videos: watch something else to decide whether to bother, then watch this to actually do it.
who_for: Business owners who have decided to try Claude and want the shortest path from signup to a working setup.
skip_if: Skip if you need convincing first - there is no case-making here, just instructions. Too shallow if you want to design a serious multi-person workflow.

title: Master Claude for Excel in 10 Minutes: Financial Modeling
author: Ali H. Salem
summary: Claude's Excel add-in reads a whole workbook and traces formulas across tabs, which is a genuinely different thing from pasting numbers into a chat. This is the clearest demonstration of that - building and auditing a financial model in the spreadsheet itself, with the formula reasoning visible rather than hidden.
who_for: Anyone who lives in spreadsheets - founders doing their own numbers, analysts, finance staff - who wants Claude working inside Excel.
skip_if: Skip if you do not use Excel or have no paid Claude plan, since the add-in requires one. Skip if your spreadsheets are simple lists rather than models - this is aimed at financial modelling.
